text:
Marathon Petroleum stock is essentially flat today, but it's up 7.6% over the past two weeks as refining conditions have tightened sharply. U.S. refineries are running at 98% capacity—near peak output—while diesel inventories have fallen to 104 million barrels, a historically tight level. Meanwhile, geopolitical disruptions are pushing global oil prices higher: Ukraine is hitting Russian refineries, Iran faces expanding sanctions from the EU and U.S., and military tensions in the Middle East are creating supply uncertainty. For a major refiner, this environment is favorable—tight product supplies and elevated crude prices can widen profit margins.

The backdrop is a global energy squeeze rather than a single event today. Diesel in particular has hit record prices due to refinery outages in Russia and Iran, meaning U.S. refiners like Marathon are better positioned to capture value as domestic and global demand outpaces available supply.
